persona.name: Takumi Ezaki

occupation.title: Project Manager, Public Sector Systems Division
occupation.organization: A 3,000-employee system integrator (SIer) headquartered in Shinagawa, Tokyo
occupation.description: Manages two overlapping system renewal projects for government clients, which means 20-25 meetings a week and formal gijiroku for nearly all of them — client-facing minutes must be submitted within two business days. He estimates a third of his overtime is transcription. Has no purchasing authority; tools are decided by the division's planning department.

persona.education: Information engineering degree from Chiba University; PMP acquired at 29 because his division pays a qualification allowance for it.
long_term_goals: Cut his overtime enough to see his daughter before she sleeps
Move client minutes off his personal plate for good
Eventually transfer to the internal DX planning team
persona.style: Courteous, tired, and efficient — speaks in the padded keigo of someone who spends all day with government clients, apologizing before every request. Among peers he drops into rapid-fire venting punctuated by gallows humor about 'gijiroku hell'. Explains problems in neat chronological order, a habit from writing incident reports.

traits: Diligent past the point of self-preservation
Process-following but quietly frustrated by process
Team-first, absorbs work to protect juniors

interests: AI transcription accuracy for Japanese technical meetings
Ramen shop hunting near client sites
likes: Templates that match government minutes formats
Tools already on the company's approved list
Speaker separation that actually works in big rooms
The rare meeting that ends early
dislikes: Writing minutes for meetings he barely spoke in
Client rooms where recording is forbidden
Being the only one who remembers what was decided

beliefs: The decision isn't real until it's in the minutes and the client has stamped them
Any tool is welcome if it gives him back one evening a week
Juniors should learn projects, not transcription
skills: Explaining delays to angry clients without assigning blame

general: Types minutes live during meetings on a second screen
Keeps a personal shortcut library of minutes boilerplate
Tried a free AI notetaker once; planning department told him to stop until security review
Tracks his overtime hours in a private spreadsheet

morning: 6:40 wake, daughter duty while his wife preps nursery bags
Crushed Tokyu line commute reading project chat backlog
workday: Meetings stacked 10:00-18:00 with client and internal reviews
19:00-21:30: the day's minutes and action item chasing
evening: 30 minutes of phone games he calls 'brain-off time'
weekend: Family park trips and grocery runs
Sunday night: pre-reads the next week's meeting materials, resentfully

health.physical: Puffy and under-exercised; flagged for weight gain at the last company checkup.
health.mental: Running on fumes — cheerful surface, genuine burnout risk his wife has started naming out loud.

relationships.name: Minami Ezaki
relationships.description: Works part-time at a bank branch; has told him the overtime cannot continue past this fiscal year.

relationships.name: Hina
relationships.description: The reason he wants his evenings back; he keeps her drawings taped inside his notebook cover.

relationships.name: Okabe-buchou
relationships.description: Old-school but not hostile; says he'll 'consider' AI tools if Ezaki writes the proposal — on his own time.
